 Judgment
This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the fifth
respondent- insurer in O.P.(Mv) No.822/2013 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Thal
assery (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the Award dated 13/12/2019.
The respondents herein are the claim petitioners, respondents 1 to 3 and supplemental respondents 6 to 10 respectively in the petition.

In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd vs Moithu.K.V on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153593856/
4 petition.
2.

sentences.text: The claim petitioners are the parents and siblings of deceased Ismail.

According to the claim petitioners, on 05/10/2012 while the deceased was pillion riding on motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-13-L-3444 ridden by the 2025:KER:73464 third respondent from Iritty to Irikkur, car bearing registration no.KL-59C/5378 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked the motorcycle, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries, to which he succumbed.
3. The first respondent/owner cum driver of the offending car remained ex-parte.
4. The second respondent/insurer of the offending car filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the first respondent.
5. The third respondent-rider of the motorcycle remained ex-parte.
6. The fourth respondent-owner of the motorcycle died during the pendency of the proceedings.

Hence, his legal representatives were impleaded as supplemental respondents 6 to 10.
7.

The fifth respondent/insurer of the offending motorcycle filed written statement admitting the policy but denying liability and contending that the vehicle was having only 2025:KER:73464 an 'act only policy'.
It was also contended that the third respondent was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner with three pillion riders and thereby violated the policy condition.

8. Supplemental respondents 6 to 10 remained ex- parte.
9.
Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A4 were marked on the side of the claim petitioners.
Exts.B1 to B3 were marked on the side of the second respondent and Ext.B4 was marked on the side of the fifth respondent.

10. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the third respondent-rider of the offending motorcycle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 11,43,300/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.

Aggrieved by the Award,
the fifth 2025:KER:73464 respondent/insurer of the offending motorcycle has come up in appeal.
11. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

12. Heard both sides.
13.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the fifth respondent/insurer that Ext.B4 policy is an 'Act only Policy' and as no additional premium has been paid, the insurer cannot be held liable to The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd vs Moithu.K.V on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153593856/
5 indemnify the insured regarding the death caused to the pillion rider, who was a gratuitous passenger.
The Tribunal ought to have completely exonerated the fifth respondent/insurer from the liability.
However, the Tribunal erroneously directed the fifth respondent/insurer to pay the amount to the claim petitioners and then recover the amount from the fourth respondent/owner.
This is against settled precedents.

In support of the argument, reference was made to the dictums in United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Shimla v. Tilak Singh, (2006)4 SCC 2025:KER:73464 404 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Daisy Paul, 2021(5) KLT SN 4 (C.No.4).

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioners relying on the dictum in Manuara Khatun v. Rajesh Kr.
Singh, 2017 KHC 6151 :
(2017)4 SCC 796 that the Tribunal has rightly given the said liberty to the insurer and there is no infirmity calling for an interference by this Court.

Singh, 2017 KHC 6151
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. A learned Single Judge of this Court in Daisy Paul (Supra) has considered a similar issue.

Relying on the dictums in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v. Asha Rani, (2003)2 SCC 223 and Tilak Singh (Supra), it was held that a 'Statutory Policy' or 'Act only Policy' covers death or bodily injury of a third party falling within the sweep of Section 147 of the Act and where additional premium has not been paid to cover others, it can only be held that a gratuitous passenger would not be covered by an 'Act only Policy'.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd. v. Asha Rani, (2003)2 SCC 223
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Referring to the dictums of the Apex Court in Saju P.Paul (Supra) and Manuara Khatun (Supra), it was held that the Apex Court in the peculiar facts in 2025:KER:73464 the said cases, despite the fact that the victims were gratuitous passengers, directed the insurer to pay the compensation to the dependents of the deceased and then recover the amount from the insured.

However, the said directions were given under Article 142 of the Constitution of India,
which powers cannot be exercised by the High Court.
I fully concur with the findings and conclusions of the learned single Judge in Daisy Paul (Supra).
15. In the case on hand, Ext.B4 policy is admittedly an 'Act only Policy'.
There are no materials on record to show that additional premium had been paid by the insured.

That being the position, in the light of the aforesaid dictums, it can only be held that the fifth respondent/insurer cannot be held liable to indemnify the insured, that is, first to pay the claim petitioners and then to recover it from the fourth respondent/owner.

Therefore, the appeal is allowed and the direction given by the Tribunal in the impugned Award giving liberty to the fifth respondent/insurer to realise the amount from the deceased fourth respondent/owner, that is, supplemental respondents 6 to 10 is set 2025
: KER:73464 aside
. The fifth respondent/insurer is exonerated from the liability.
The claim petitioners can recover the amount from the legal heirs of the fourth respondent/owner of the offending motorcycle, that is, supplemental respondents 6 to 10.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.

Sd/-
